interpretation.reproduced: All five mappings were observed live on three separate occasions (2026-11-17 in the prior sessions, and twice on 2026-11-20 by sessions arena-23d7ed19 and arena-82d39deb), each agreeing 5/5 — so FLG-008 stayed closed and the observed_* fields rest on three matching observations rather than single-session noise. A fourth re-resolution on 2026-11-20 by session arena-9a3bb152 matched only 1 of 5: B0f3GKalj reproduced its recorded target, while the other four tokens landed on the Amazon homepage. That divergence is published as FLG-026 with the action that would settle it; it does not by itself invalidate any link (FLG-003).
interpretation.what_reproduction_does_not_prove: Every final URL in the first three observations carried lv=shuf (shuffle) and plpRedirect=mhFallback (listing-page fallback). That is a fallback route, not a canonical resolution of the submitted token. The targets were stable per token across the first three observations, so they are a usable observation — but they do not confirm that the person who supplied the links intended these five products, and the fourth observation shows the behavior is not guaranteed to reproduce from every client. Intended fields therefore stay blank.
interpretation.operational_consequence: Keep publishing without reader links until the Associates one-link test (FLG-002) confirms destination and tracking report. If the owner confirms the five products are the intended ones, nothing about the pages changes except the intended_* fields and confirmation_date. Third observation also re-read each listing's product-details table: one recorded row was wrong (the 8-quart Chefman's wattage — FLG-022, corrected) and four listing-internal contradictions were confirmed (FLG-005, FLG-010, FLG-018, FLG-020). Fourth observation (FLG-026): destination must be re-checked from a normal browser and inside the enrolled Associates workflow test (FLG-002) before any short link is used at scale.
